text: If Earth stopped spinning, you wouldn't.
Right now, you're moving. Near the equator, about sixteen hundred kilometres an hour.
asr: Right now, you're moving. Near the equator, about 1600 kilometers an hour.

text: You don't feel it, because everything moves with you.
So if the planet stopped in one second, all of that would keep going.
You, your house, the trees. Anything not stuck to solid rock gets thrown east.
The air keeps going too. A wind faster than any tornado, across most of the planet.
And the oceans keep going, crashing over the land.
Now say Earth survived that. What would a still planet be like?
One sunrise a year. Six months of daylight, then six months of night.
The day side bakes. The night side freezes.
Then the oceans move. Spinning makes Earth bulge at the middle, and the water piles up there.
Without it, the water drains to the poles, leaving one huge continent around the middle.
Earth's magnetic shield could weaken too, letting in more of the Sun's radiation.
The good news: nothing can stop Earth that fast.
The weird news: it's already slowing down. Every century, our day gets about two thousandths of a second longer.
And what's braking it? The Moon. The same Moon that's slowly leaving us.
asr: And what's breaking it? The Moon. The same Moon that's slowly leaving us.

text: So don't worry. You've got billions of years before you need to hold on.
